title: Rigveda 10.119: The song of the drunken Indra (Laba)
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.119: The song of the drunken Indra (Laba): Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.119 is a hymn of 13 verses addressed to soliloquy of one intoxicated by Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 106r-106v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.119.1-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 6, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 106r
translation.original_text:
1iti̱ vā iti̍ me̱ mano̱ gām aśva̍ṁ sanuyā̱m iti̍ | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
2pra vātā̍ iva̱ dodha̍ta̱ un mā̍ pī̱tā a̍yaṁsata | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
3un mā̍ pī̱tā a̍yaṁsata̱ ratha̱m aśvā̍ ivā̱śava̍ḥ | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
4upa̍ mā ma̱tir a̍sthita vā̱śrā pu̱tram i̍va pri̱yam | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
5a̱haṁ taṣṭe̍va va̱ndhura̱m pary a̍cāmi hṛ̱dā ma̱tim | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
translation.text:
1THIS, even this was my resolve, to win a cow, to win a steed: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
2Like violent gusts of wind the draughts that I have drunk have lifted me Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
3The draughts I drank have borne me up, as fleet-foot horses draw a car: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
4The hymn hath reached me, like a cow who lows to meet her darling calf: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
5As a wright bends a chariot-seat so round my heart I bend the hymn: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 106r (OPenn image 105, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.118.7 ‹śociṣāgne rakṣas tvaṁ daha›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 106v, begins in RV 10.119.6 ‹-somasyāpām iti›. Verses 10.119.1-5 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.119.6-13 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 6, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 106v
translation.original_text:
6na̱hi me̍ akṣi̱pac ca̱nācchā̍ntsu̱ḥ pañca̍ kṛ̱ṣṭaya̍ḥ | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
7na̱hi me̱ roda̍sī u̱bhe a̱nyam pa̱kṣaṁ ca̱na prati̍ | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
8a̱bhi dyām ma̍hi̱nā bhu̍vam a̱bhī̱3̱̍mām pṛ̍thi̱vīm ma̱hīm | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
9hantā̱ham pṛ̍thi̱vīm i̱māṁ ni da̍dhānī̱ha ve̱ha vā̍ | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
10o̱ṣam it pṛ̍thi̱vīm a̱haṁ ja̱ṅghanā̍nī̱ha ve̱ha vā̍ | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
11di̱vi me̍ a̱nyaḥ pa̱kṣo̱3̱̍ 'dho a̱nyam a̍cīkṛṣam | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
12a̱ham a̍smi mahāma̱ho̍ 'bhina̱bhyam udī̍ṣitaḥ | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
13gṛ̱ho yā̱my ara̍ṁkṛto de̱vebhyo̍ havya̱vāha̍naḥ | ku̱vit soma̱syāpā̱m iti̍ ||
translation.text:
6Not as a mote within the eye count the Five Tribes of men with me: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
7The heavens and earth themselves have not grown equal to one half of me Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
8I in my grandeur have surpassed the heavens and all this spacious earth Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
9Aha! this spacious earth will I deposit either here or there Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
10In one short moment will I smite the earth in fury here or there: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
11One of my flanks is in the sky; I let the other trail below: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
12I, greatest of the Mighty Ones, am lifted to the firmament: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
13I seek the worshipper's abode; oblation-bearer to the Gods: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 106v (OPenn image 106, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.119.6 ‹-somasyāpām iti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 107r, begins in RV 10.120.1 ‹-śatrūn anu yaṁ viśve›. Verses 10.119.6-13 end on this page; 10.119.6 begins on fol. 106r.
